overall: Both concerns from the insufficient-context remediation review are closed by candidate 90aa205219f0defba1ec649d7dd025f31b8c0199. The timeout path measures exact process liveness and recomputes Owner-checkout identity before writing candidate-preserving procedural evidence; the store then revalidates the started-process shape and stage consistency. A blocking report with a non-zero process exit remains technical because the non-zero-exit procedural override applies only to an otherwise accepted report, and write-time and replay-time acceptance must remain identical. Outcome mismatch tests cover procedural evidence presented as passed or technical, and aggregate, empty-gate, stage-consistency, liveness, and checkout-drift regressions remain fail closed. The review does not establish release readiness, authentication, host write confinement, or publication/install.

risks: Hosts without a usable process identity source can degrade liveness to uncertain and block every security review.
Scanner stdout and stderr remain buffered without an explicit byte ceiling, so a hostile or excessively chatty scanner can consume local memory.
A boundary-unsafe ending consumes the admission but deliberately writes no candidate-preserving evidence, requiring operator recovery.
Replay revalidates report and command self-consistency after the temporary proof root is gone; same-user state remains cooperative identity rather than authentication.
If process identity construction ever returned null instead of raising, the main path would fail with an unstructured exception rather than a false accept.
